span.label: null-result
span.quote: Despite extensive testing, we found no evidence that unconsciously perceived words can activate sensorimotor processes, although these words are processed up to the semantic level.

span.label: masked semantic priming by spatial words
span.quote: In six experiments we investigated the nature of masked semantic priming using words referring to the vertical spatial axis (e.g., up, down).

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: In six experiments we progressively excluded the possibility that action modulation by subliminal words could be explained by (i) short-term stimulus-response associations, (ii) symbolic relationships between prime and targets or (iii) the Evidence Accumulation mechanism.

span.quote: Future studies are needed to determine whether negative semantic priming like that observed by Dudschig and colleagues is a signature of embodied mechanisms or can be entirely explained in symbolic terms.

span.quote: The critical finding is that when symbolic and nonsemantic mechanisms were prevented, allowing only for a genuinely embodied semantic priming, no effect was found. Conversely, facilitation emerged in the same experimental paradigm when embodied priming was prevented and symbolic priming was allowed

span.label: conscious access
span.quote: We thus conclude that sensorimotor activations might need conscious access to emerge during language understanding

span.label: **A NULL WITH ITS OWN POSITIVE CONTROL, IN THE SAME APPARATUS:** `when symbolic and nonsemantic mechanisms were prevented, allowing only for a genuinely EMBODIED semantic priming, NO EFFECT WAS FOUND. Conversely, FACILITATION EMERGED IN THE SAME EXPERIMENTAL PARADIGM when embodied priming was prevented and symbolic priming was allowed.` **Six experiments, and the machine works when you leave the other route open.** A failed manipulation cannot selectively succeed - which is the objection every unconscious-priming null has to answer, and this one answers it by construction rather than by argument. Same structure as hesselmann2016 (Q-818) at three times the scale
span.quote: The critical finding is that when symbolic and nonsemantic mechanisms were prevented, allowing only for a genuinely embodied semantic priming, no effect was found. Conversely, facilitation emerged in the same experimental paradigm when embodied priming was prevented and symbolic priming was allowed

span.label: **AND THE LEVEL CLAIM IS EXACT:** `we found NO EVIDENCE that unconsciously perceived words can activate SENSORIMOTOR processes, ALTHOUGH THESE WORDS ARE PROCESSED UP TO THE SEMANTIC LEVEL.` **Unconscious words reach meaning and stop before simulation.** The `although` is the whole value: this is not a claim that unconscious processing is shallow - the words got to semantics - but that the chain BREAKS at a specific link. A corpus of masked-priming records mostly argues about whether meaning was reached at all; this one grants that and asks what comes after
span.quote: we found no evidence that unconsciously perceived words can activate sensorimotor processes, although these words are processed up to the semantic level

span.label: **AND THE CONCLUSION IS OFFERED AS A CONDITION, NOT A MECHANISM:** `We thus conclude that sensorimotor activations MIGHT NEED CONSCIOUS ACCESS to emerge during language understanding.` `might need` is inside the quote. **What makes this more than a hedge is that it is falsifiable in an obvious way** - show sensorimotor activation from an unconscious word under any conditions and it is gone - and the authors have just spent six experiments failing to do that themselves
span.quote: We thus conclude that sensorimotor activations might need conscious access to emerge during language understanding

span.label: **AND IT SITS AGAINST dehaene1998 IN THIS CORPUS, WITHOUT CONTRADICTING IT.** dehaene1998 concluded that an unreportable numeral was `unconsciously processed according to task instructions, ALL THE WAY DOWN TO THE MOTOR SYSTEM`. This paper finds no sensorimotor activation from unconscious words at all. **Both can be right, because `reaches the motor system` names two things:** dehaene1998's is a TRAINED RESPONSE MAPPING - a digit compared to 5, a hand prepared, an arbitrary rule applied - and Bottini's is SIMULATION OF MEANING, the claim that understanding `up` re-enacts upward experience. An unconscious stimulus can drive the first and fail the second. **Same shape as Q-821's two senses of `nonconscious`, and the corpus currently indexes both pairs under one heading**
span.quote: we found no evidence that unconsciously perceived words can activate sensorimotor processes, although these words are processed up to the semantic level

span.label: contradicts → Dudschig et al. (2014)
span.quote: It is interesting to note that, although these data can be interpreted as consistent with embodied semantics, they are at odds with those reported by Dudschig et al. (2014), who used a similar paradigm: We found a facilitation effect, whereas these authors reported negative priming, that is, incongruent prime-response pairs led to faster RTs compared to congruent ones.

span.label: contradicts → the elaborate processing hypothesis (Kunde, Kiesel, & Hoffmann, 2003)
span.quote: However, our results stand in contrast to what has been called the “elaborate processing hypothesis” (Kunde, Kiesel, & Hoffmann, 2003), according to which conscious and unconscious words undergo the same levels of semantic processing.

span.label: contradicts → radical theories of Embodied Semantics
span.quote: These results challenge radical theories of Embodied Semantics by showing that there is no evidence that unconsciously perceived words activate motor programs solely on the basis of their long-term meaning.

Weight 0.95: explicit in the quote, and the design exists for nothing else.
